candidates.hint: Strongest all-round engineer: state of the art on agentic coding, terminal and computer use, research, and math, and token-efficient per task despite the price. Communicates clearly and needs little rework. Use medium for single-shot review, analysis, and bounded changes; high for long autonomous tool loops, where it wastes fewer turns; xhigh/max only when high has measurably failed on hard architecture or debugging.

Fast and cheap, yet a competent agent when the task is well specified: routine features, local bugs, tests, scripts, formatting, translation, summaries. Use off for trivial single-step work, high as the default when it must explore, edit several files, or verify, and xhigh when a bounded task still needs extra care. Do not push it into ambiguous architecture, security, or subtle concurrency work; escalate instead.

Anthropic's top generally available model for long-horizon autonomous work: multi-hour agentic coding, deep research, exacting code review, front-end polish, and the best independent reasoning scores. Takes a brief and runs to completion with little check-in, so it suits well-briefed large tasks over interactive back-and-forth. Safeguards may refuse security or exploit-adjacent work; route that to Opus. Start at high; xhigh/max only when Opus 5 at xhigh would still fall short.

Anthropic's recommended starting point for complex agentic coding: deep reasoning, large multi-file refactors and migrations, obscure root causes, and high-stakes or irreversible changes, with strong self-verification and judgment. Pauses at natural checkpoints, so it fits ambiguous, collaborative work better than Fable. Converts extra effort into results reliably: start at high, xhigh for the most demanding work, max rarely. Prose is dense; avoid for writing-heavy tasks.

Best-value Claude and the Claude Code default: strong on everyday coding, bug fixes, tests, refactors, CI triage, and long terminal or tool sequences, and it checks its own output unprompted. Trails Opus on the hardest long-horizon problems, ambiguous architecture, and image-heavy code tasks; escalate when a task needs several correct judgment calls in a row. Prefer xhigh; max for unusually difficult work.

Fast, economical model for everyday coding, repository exploration, and automation. Use off for summaries, low for simple edits, high for multi-step work, and max for harder bounded tasks at the cost of longer reasoning.
